title: Residential Painting in High Springs, FL
description: Residential painting in High Springs, FL for craftsman bungalows, clapboard homes, and newer houses in Bridlewood and Bailey Estates. Written warranty.
h1: Residential Painting in High Springs, FL
heroIntro: Repainting High Springs homes inside and out, from older clapboard near downtown to newer houses in Bridlewood and Bailey Estates.

sections.h2: Two very different kinds of homes
body: Residential painting in High Springs, FL mostly falls into two groups. The first is the older wood homes around Historic Downtown, with clapboard walls, wide porch trim, and window casings that have been painted many times. The second is newer homes in Bridlewood and Bailey Estates, where the work is more typical: tired builder paint, scuffed hallways, and caulk that has started to split.
Both get the same company and the same warranty, but the prep looks very different. More on the town is on our High Springs painting contractor page.

On a craftsman home, the trim is a big part of its appeal. We scrape back to a sound edge and feather-sand the transitions so old paint layers don't show as ridges. We prime bare wood the same day so it doesn't soak up moisture overnight. Caulk goes where joints actually move, not over decorative profiles. Rotted sills and boards are replaced with matching profiles where possible, and every replacement is listed on the estimate before the work begins. Our article on cracked paint on window frames explains why sills are worth fixing early.

In newer houses, the focus is on finishes that hold up. We use washable satin where kids and pets rub the walls, waterborne urethane enamel on doors and trim, and fresh caulk around tubs and counters. Outside, flat builder paint on stucco and siding gets two full coats of 100% acrylic or elastomeric, depending on the surface.

sections.h2: Living at home during the project
body: You don't need to move out. Inside, crews work room by room, moving and covering furniture and cleaning up each evening. Outside, plantings and walkways are protected and rinsed. Low-VOC products are available for bedrooms. A single room usually takes a day, a full interior three days to two weeks, and a full exterior three to seven working days plus washing and dry time. The High Springs exterior page and interior page cover each side in more detail, and our main residential painting page explains the general approach.

faqs.q: Will you replace rotted trim on my older home?
faqs.a: Yes. Rotted trim, fascia, and sills are replaced instead of painted over, matched to the existing profile where possible, and listed on the estimate before work begins.

faqs.q: Should I paint inside or outside first?
faqs.a: Many people do the interior in summer and the exterior from October through May, when drying conditions are best. If you want both done at once, we can schedule them together.

faqs.q: What do I get when the job is finished?
faqs.a: A punch walk you sign, labelled touch-up paint, and a written workmanship warranty on top of the manufacturer's coverage, up to 10 years on exterior work.

faqs.q: Do you paint porch ceilings and floors?
faqs.a: Yes. Porch ceilings, columns, rails, and floors can all be included, each with the right coating for how it's used.
